decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY covering code-used and no-code ticket visibility and historical backfill.
The source changes accounting and metadata behavior, not FAQ copy; the existing FAQ state already says no-referral commissions and tickets go to a random holder.
Reward-accounting visibility for primary mints does not change which NFT state transfers on a secondary sale.
The source explicitly concerns primary-mint ticket and commission accounting and does not alter secondary-sale royalties.
The source does not change which successfully minted NFTs are counted as owned by the connected user.
The count of twelve completed mints is contextual evidence for reward accounting, not a change to the public mint-count rule.
Ticket and commission projection does not change the collection's unlimited-mint model.
NFT reward attributes are distinct from the sizing and visibility of the book-cover image.
The source does not alter the View Book action, its label, or its ownership-based visibility.

The source requires randomly assigned no-referral commissions to appear on the leaderboard and NFT attributes, requires historical omissions to be reconciled, and establishes one $5 commission for each issued ticket.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
At this point, we have completed 12 mints, so that should amount to 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**Even if no referral code is used, a ticket and commission are still issued**.

Currently, **when a code is used**, it is accurately reflected on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

If **no referral code is used**, the ticket and commission are assigned at random.
(B**ut they must still be reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I believe that since your most recent fix, the randomly assigned tickets from the last 2 mints have been reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
However, the missing tickets have not been backfilled.

The commissions from these purchases without a code are also still not reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot, you will see that I have an NFT showing 2 tickets but only 1 x $5 commission. That should not be possible because each ticket includes a $5 commission.

Also, in my leaderboard screenshot, only 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions are accounted for out of 12 total mints.
Whether or not a referral code is used, 12 mints should result in 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions.

value_updates.no_code_commission_projection: Randomly assigned $5 commissions from no-referral mints must be reflected on the dashboard, leaderboard, and in NFT attributes.
value_updates.ticket_commission_consistency_rule: Every issued ticket corresponds to one $5 commission, so ticket and commission totals must remain consistent.

decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY establishing one $5 commission for every primary mint, including no-referral mints; its random-recipient policy was already present.
The source confirms code-used accounting visibility but does not change the NFT mint number used as its referral-code identity.
